title: Come to Jesus, O My Brothers
description: Come to Jesus, O My Brothers in Tonic Solfa to ST. AUSTIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 161, “The Weary and Heavy-Laden”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.4.7 (8.7.8.7.4.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AUSTIN; any other 8.7.8.7.4.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come to Je-sus, O my broth-ers, Come in this ac-cept-ed hour; Je-sus rea-dy stands to save you, Full of pi-ty, love, and power; He is ab-le, He is will-ing, doubt no more.

lines: Come to Jesus, O my brothers,
Jesus ready stands to save you,
Full of pity, love, and power;
He is willing, — doubt no more.
Let not conscience make you linger,
Is to feel your need of him;
If you tarry till you're better,
You will never come at all.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AUSTIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
